lib-22.authors: Hendrik G. Roozen, Ranne de Waart, Petra J. A. van der Kroft
lib-22.takeaway: CRAFT, which coaches family members, was better at getting resistant loved ones into treatment than Al-Anon or confrontational interventions.

lib-22.title: Psychosocial adjustment of adult children of alcoholics
lib-22.takeaway: Harter's review found adult children of alcoholics vary widely and many do not show a distinct profile, which questions fixed family survival roles.

lib-25.title: The Effectiveness of Interventions Intended to Improve Employment Outcomes for Persons with Substance Use Disorder: An Updated Systematic Review
lib-25.takeaway: This updated review found some employment interventions for people with substance use disorders help, with Individual Placement and Support showing the most evidence.

lib-25.title: Employment After Prison: A Longitudinal Study of Former Prisoners
lib-25.authors: Christy A. Visher, Sara Debus-Sherrill, Jennifer Yahner
lib-25.takeaway: In this study of people leaving prison, prior work history and connection to employers before release improved employment, while quick relapse lowered it.

lib-25.title: Vocational Interests and Performance: A Quantitative Summary of Over 60 Years of Research
lib-25.authors: Christopher D. Nye, Rong Su, James Rounds, et al.
lib-25.takeaway: This meta-analysis found that matching vocational interests to work predicted performance and persistence, supporting the session's interest-matching.

lib-25.title: Work as a Turning Point in the Life Course of Criminals: A Duration Model of Age, Employment, and Recidivism
lib-25.takeaway: In a job program experiment, work reduced crime for people 27 and older but had little effect for younger participants, so jobs are not a turning point for everyone.

lib-26.title: Advisor-Teller Money Manager (ATM) Therapy for Substance Use Disorders
lib-26.authors: Marc I. Rosen, Bruce J. Rounsaville, Karen M. Ablondi, et al.
lib-26.takeaway: In Advisor-Teller Money Manager therapy, money management tied to recovery goals reduced cocaine use among people with psychiatric illness.

lib-26.title: Does Financial Education Impact Financial Literacy and Financial Behavior, and If So, When?
lib-26.takeaway: Financial education improved financial knowledge and behavior, especially when intense and offered at a 'teachable moment'.

lib-26.title: Financial Literacy, Financial Education, and Downstream Financial Behaviors
lib-26.authors: Daniel von der Heyde Fernandes, John G. Lynch, Richard G. Netemeyer
lib-26.takeaway: This meta-analysis found financial education explained very little of later financial behavior and its effects faded with time.

lib-26.title: The relationship between personal unsecured debt and mental and physical health: A systematic review and meta-analysis
lib-26.authors: Thomas Hugh Richardson, Peter Elliott, Ronald Roberts
lib-26.takeaway: Debt was consistently linked to worse mental and physical health, though causality is unclear.

lib-27.title: The relationship between personal unsecured debt and mental and physical health: A systematic review and meta-analysis
lib-27.authors: Thomas Hugh Richardson, Peter Elliott, Ronald Roberts
lib-27.takeaway: Unsecured debt was associated with worse mental health, including substance-related problems, supporting attention to credit and debt.

lib-27.title: Does Financial Education Impact Financial Literacy and Financial Behavior, and If So, When?
lib-27.takeaway: Financial education is most effective as intensive, timely instruction, which fits a dedicated credit and insurance lesson.

lib-27.title: Financial Literacy, Financial Education, and Downstream Financial Behaviors
lib-27.authors: Daniel von der Heyde Fernandes, John G. Lynch, Richard G. Netemeyer
lib-27.takeaway: Financial education's effects were small and short-lived; 'just-in-time' help tied to a specific decision may work better.

lib-30.title: The relationship between substance misuse and complicated grief: A systematic review
lib-30.authors: Anna B. Parisi, Anjalee Sharma, Matthew O. Howard, et al.
lib-30.takeaway: This review found complicated grief and substance misuse often go together and that grief interventions reduced both.

lib-30.title: Beyond Abstinence: Changes in Indices of Quality of Life with Time in Recovery in a Nationally Representative Sample of U.S. Adults
lib-30.authors: John Francis Kelly, M. Claire Greene, Brandon G. Bergman
lib-30.takeaway: In a national sample, quality of life improved with time in recovery, though self-esteem and happiness dipped in the first year, matching 'what sobriety costs'.

lib-30.title: THE DUAL PROCESS MODEL OF COPING WITH BEREAVEMENT: RATIONALE AND DESCRIPTION
lib-30.takeaway: The dual process model says healthy grieving moves back and forth between facing the loss and rebuilding life, including taking breaks from grief.

lib-30.title: Loss, Trauma, and Human Resilience: Have We Underestimated the Human Capacity to Thrive After Extremely Aversive Events?
lib-30.takeaway: Bonanno shows resilience after loss is common, so not everyone needs to work through a long grief process.

lib-31.title: An Empirical Examination of the Stage Theory of Grief
lib-31.authors: Paul K. Maciejewski, Baohui Zhang, Susan D. Block, et al.
lib-31.takeaway: This study of bereaved people found negative grief indicators peaked within about six months and acceptance was the most common response, offering partial support for a sequence.

lib-31.title: Cautioning Health-Care Professionals: Bereaved Persons Are Misguided Through the Stages of Grief
lib-31.authors: Margaret Stroebe, Henk A. W. Schut, Kathrin Boerner
lib-31.venue: OMEGA - Journal of Death and Dying
lib-31.takeaway: Stroebe and colleagues argue the five-stage theory lacks scientific support and can mislead grieving people, and urge professionals to replace it with better models.

lib-31.title: Loss, Trauma, and Human Resilience: Have We Underestimated the Human Capacity to Thrive After Extremely Aversive Events?
lib-31.takeaway: Bonanno shows that resilience is a common response to loss, so many people do not move through the stages at all and should not be told they must.

lib-31.title: The relationship between substance misuse and complicated grief: A systematic review
lib-31.authors: Anna B. Parisi, Anjalee Sharma, Matthew O. Howard, et al.
lib-31.takeaway: This review links complicated grief to substance misuse and found grief interventions reduced both, supporting work on grief that use had numbed.

lib-33.title: Relapse Prevention for Alcohol and Drug Problems: That Was Zen, This Is Tao
lib-33.authors: Katie A. Witkiewitz, G. Alan Marlatt
lib-33.takeaway: Witkiewitz and Marlatt's updated model maps how distant risks and immediate triggers interact on the way to relapse, the chain this session builds a wall against.

lib-33.title: Efficacy of relapse prevention: A meta-analytic review
lib-33.authors: Jennifer E. Irvin, Clint A. Bowers, Michael E. Dunn, et al.
lib-33.venue: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
lib-33.takeaway: A meta-analysis of 26 studies found relapse prevention effective overall, particularly for alcohol problems.

lib-33.title: Drinking trajectories following an initial lapse
lib-33.authors: Katie A. Witkiewitz, Katherine E. Masyn
lib-33.takeaway: Most first lapses did not lead to heavy use, and coping predicted recovery, so a lapse is a point to intervene rather than the end of the chain.

lib-33.title: Distinctions without a difference: Direct comparisons of psychotherapies for alcohol use disorders
lib-33.authors: Zac E. Imel, Bruce E. Wampold, Scott D. Miller, et al.
lib-33.takeaway: Direct comparisons of alcohol treatments found no reliable differences between approaches, which suggests relapse prevention's specific techniques may matter less than shared factors like support and engagement.
